filename: Improving the Modeling and Analysis of Tropical Convection and Precipitation Through Machine Learning Methods.pdf
title: Improving The Modeling and Analysis of Tropical Convection and Precipitation through Machine Learning Methods
venue: Doctoral Dissertation, University of California, Irvine
processes: sub-grid vertical transport of heat and moisture
parameterization_target: atmospheric moist convection, sub-grid diabatic heating, sub-grid moistening, precipitation, and radiative fluxes
code_availability: The codebase for running the SPCAM5 simulations is archived at https://github.com/mspritch/UltraCAM-spcam2_0_cesm1_1_1; hyperparameter tuning used Sherpa (https://github.com/sherpa-ai/sherpa).
testbed_rationale: The thesis introduces and tests extensive datasets of SPCAM5 real-geography sub-grid tendencies and high-resolution CRM vertical velocity profiles, benchmarked for offline emulation and VAE analysis. The simulation code is openly available on GitHub.
pain_points: Computational expense of high-resolution storm-resolving models (SRMs) limiting runs to short durations
Exorbitant volume of SRM simulation data (petabytes), creating storage and analysis bottlenecks
Failure of feed-forward DNNs to capture fast stochastic signals in the planetary boundary layer without temporal memory or stochastic components
Drizzle bias and incorrect diurnal cycle timing of precipitation over continents in unconstrained and non-tuned DNN emulators
Offline fit skill does not guarantee online stability in prognostic coupling (hybrid models run into stability issues)
Violation of physical conservation/positivity constraints in standard unconstrained neural networks
extraction_notes: Chapter 2 explores offline emulation of SPCAM5 sub-grid parameterization using feed-forward DNNs with hyperparameter optimization and physical constraints, plus offline 1-way coupling to CLM. Chapters 3-5 focus on unsupervised learning with VAEs, clustering, and vector quantization to analyze CRM vertical velocity snapshots across SPCAM and DYAMOND models.
